why: p21's sad looped melody over booming bass and its dropout into a beat switch pull you in, while p20 floats on a pastel Cmaj7-Bm7 sway that only darkens briefly at its Fm9 peak.
p24's band crashing in at 0:21 after a clean intro gives a heavy, sad arrival, whereas p17 is a music-box lullaby rocking between two chords with only a brief ringing pause at 0:36.
p19's one-note bittersweet ostinato with drums dropping in and out and the lift at 0:54 is more immersive than p22's loud one-level F#m-E-A loop, despite p22's slam-in at 0:17.
p21 is a moody late-night beat with a dropout and beat switch at 2:40, while p17 is a sweet lullaby-like two-chord mallet sketch that barely changes beyond its pause at 0:36.

p18's dark pads swelling into a hard beat drop at 0:20 with drumless breakdowns is immersive and cool, while p23 is a heroic cinematic build from a music-box intro to a static four-bar climax at 1:08.
p25's warm late-night band groove landing at 0:40 after a hazy intro, with a drumless middle, beats p17's pastel music-box rocking that just pauses at 0:36 and drifts off.

Both are dark head-nod beats, but p18's filter-swell intro into a +10 dB drop at 0:20 and its 5-bar drumless breakdown at 2:54 breathe more than p21's wall-to-wall loop, whose best moment is the beat switch at 2:47.

p25's bittersweet bass-led groove with the band entering at 0:40 and a drumless development at 1:15 has more mood and breath than p16's bright, compressed game-cue bounce, which only turns wistful briefly around bar 23.
p19's hypnotic, bittersweet ostinato with the kit coming and going and a lift at 0:54 suits the listener better than p23's heroic crescendo into a one-loop climax at 1:08 after a music-box intro.

p25 has a real arrival when the band enters at 0:40 and a floating drumless middle at 1:15, while p19's wistful ostinato is lovely but a short, slightly tense sketch whose lift at 0:54 passes quickly.

p24's heavy, sad band crash at 0:21 after a clean intro and its emotional Bm-G-D-A turn at 1:18 hit harder than p19's small bittersweet ostinato and brief lift at 0:54, though p24's grinding riff risks feeling menacing.
p21's sad, glossy loop with drums dropping in and the filtered dropout into a beat switch at 2:40 is more immersive and nod-worthy than p19's short ostinato sketch with its lift at 0:54.
p18's dark hypnotic pads swelling into a hard drop at 0:20 and its drumless C/Ab breakdowns outclass p25's pleasant but warm, one-level band groove that enters at 0:40.
p23 at least delivers an arrival when the full texture lands 13 dB louder at 0:27, while p17 stays a gentle lullaby loop whose only event is a ringing pause at 0:36.
p23's build from near-silence at 0:26 into a drum-launched climax gives more impact than p20's swaying pastel home loop, which only darkens briefly at its Fm9 peak around 0:56.
p24's dark, heavy band crashing in at 0:21 has real weight and sadness, while p16 is a bright, bouncy game cue that stays at one loudness with only a brief wistful turn at bar 23.
p21's moody sad loop and beat switch at 2:47 beat p16's cheerful, compressed game-music bounce whose one-bar break at 0:58 barely changes the energy.
p22's full band slamming in at 0:17 gives energy and impact, while p17 is a sweet music-box lullaby loop with only a ringing pause at 0:36.
p23's crescendo from a quiet intro to a drum-launched climax around 1:08 gives an arrival p16 lacks, since p16's bright game cue sits at one level apart from its break at 0:58.
p25's bittersweet late-night groove landing at 0:40 with a drumless middle is more immersive than p20's pastel, waltz-like sway that fades quickly after its darker Fm9 stretch at 0:56.
p22's minor-key band slam at 0:17 and bright lift at 2:09 are energetic if flat, which beats p20's sweet swaying keys loop despite its darker middle at 0:56.
p24's heavy, sad band arrival at 0:21 and emotional Bm-G-D-A turn at 1:18 outweigh p20's pastel game-style sway and quick fade at 1:16.
p18's dark, hypnotic drop at 0:20 and drumless breakdowns pull you in, while p22 hammers one F#m-E-A loop at a flat, loud level after its slam-in at 0:17.
Both have big arrivals (p24's band crash at 0:21, p18's beat drop at 0:20), but p18's hypnotic melancholy and drumless breakdown at 2:54 breathe, while p24's grinding riff stays a menacing wall.
p22's minor-key slam-in at 0:17 and major lift at 2:09 drive harder than p16's cheerful, cute game-cue bounce, whose darker turn at bar 23 is brief.
